summary: Iteration 33 — End-to-end testing of the new @-mention feature on top of the Messages module. Backend: 15/15 pytest pass (4 new test_message_mentions.py + 11 prior). Frontend: full cross-role E2E validated — super_admin sends URGENT announcement to KM_BLR with mentions=[blr1] → mentioned user receives type='mention' notif with title '🔔 MUNEER MUHAMMED mentioned you · MENTION_URGENT_E2E' and link='/messages/<id>'; dashboard shows the banner-mentioned-<msgId> '@ YOU' chip + orange ring on the banner; mention-pill-<userId> renders as amber-bordered pill in thread root body. Reply composer (data-testid=reply-textarea) also triggers reply-textarea-mention-dropdown, options are thread-participants-minus-self, click inserts '@Name ' and adds id; submitted reply renders mention-pill-<userId> in the reply body. Mention auto-removal verified: deleting the '@Name' substring before send results in mentions=[] persisted server-side. Keyboard nav (ArrowDown+Enter selects, Escape closes dropdown) all work. Compose 'Highlighting 1 person — they'll get a stronger notification' label appears as expected.

critical_code_review_comments: messages.py router stays clean — _filter_mentions + _fanout_with_mentions are pure helpers that split fan-out cleanly (mention set excluded from standard batch, no double-notify). Both batches preserve link='/messages/<id>'.

_filter_mentions correctly de-dupes via dict.fromkeys and intersects with the resolved recipient set — sender id is automatically excluded because _resolve_recipients drops the actor before _filter_mentions runs.

MentionTextarea + MentionBody (frontend) cleanly separate rendering vs editing. The data-testid='mention-pill-<userId>' contract is honored. Useful enhancement (future): consider also matching mention pills by name fallback when ids drift, but current strict-id matching avoids false positives.

Note: AnnouncementBanners uses the MESSAGE id in banner-mentioned-<id> (not the user id). The problem statement was ambiguous on this; the code's choice is sensible (one chip per banner). Action item only if main agent intended otherwise.

Banner 5-cap interacts with mentions: an urgent banner-with-mention can still be hidden if 5 other urgent banners precede it. Current sort is urgent-first, newest-first — a mention-aware sort (mentioned-me first) would surface @-you banners reliably. NON-BLOCKING enhancement, but worth flagging since the original spec said 'Tagged users would get a stronger highlight … even if they've already read the parent thread.'
Regression intact: compose/list/sent/kind filters/dismiss/mark-read/reply/delete-thread all still work (verified earlier iter_32, no changes to those paths).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Mention feature is production-ready across backend + frontend. The only nuance to remember: AnnouncementBanners testid is 'banner-mentioned-<MESSAGE_ID>' (not the user id) — applies the orange ring + '@ You' chip when current user appears in banner.mentions[]. To reliably see the chip in a UI test, either dismiss other urgent banners first OR send the mention as priority='urgent' to a freshly seeded user with no other banners. Optional enhancement worth flagging to main agent: re-sort banners so 'I'm-mentioned-here' rows surface above non-mention urgents (current sort can hide a mention banner behind the 5-cap).
